name: Abducens nucleus
summary: The abducens nucleus lies under the facial colliculus in the caudal pons and is the horizontal gaze center's output stage: its motor neurons supply the ipsilateral lateral rectus, and its internuclear neurons cross in the MLF to drive the contralateral medial rectus. Because both cell types live together, a nuclear lesion causes a conjugate gaze palsy toward the side of the lesion, not an isolated lateral rectus palsy. The facial nerve fibers loop around it, so a nuclear lesion often adds an ipsilateral facial palsy.

anatomy.location: Dorsal caudal pons beneath the facial colliculus of the fourth ventricular floor, paramedian, with the PPRF just anterior and lateral to it and the MLF medial to it.

function: Abduction of the ipsilateral eye and, through internuclear neurons, conjugate horizontal gaze to the ipsilateral side; final common pathway for saccades, pursuit and the vestibulo-ocular reflex in the horizontal plane.

bestView.label: facial colliculus level of the caudal pons
floor of the fourth ventricle at the facial colliculus

imaging.normalAppearance: Not resolved on routine MRI; the facial colliculus is the paramedian bump on the floor of the fourth ventricle at the caudal pons. Small lesions here are best seen on thin axial FLAIR or DWI.

pathology.pathology: Pontine tegmental infarct or demyelination at the facial colliculus
pathology.finding: Small paramedian dorsal pontine lesion with ipsilateral gaze palsy and lower motor neuron facial weakness.
Mass in the dorsal pons displacing the ventricular floor; sixth nerve and gaze palsies are early signs.

lesionEffects.deficit: Conjugate horizontal gaze palsy toward the side of the lesion
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of both motor and internuclear neurons

lesionEffects.deficit: Ipsilateral lower motor neuron facial palsy
lesionEffects.mechanism: Facial nerve genu looping over the nucleus
Abducens fascicle or nerve, not the nucleus

examination: Ask the patient to follow a target to each side: nuclear lesions stop both eyes at the midline
Test the vestibulo-ocular reflex (doll's eyes) — absent toward the lesion side in nuclear lesions, preserved in PPRF lesions
pearls: A gaze palsy that cannot be overcome by the oculocephalic reflex is nuclear; one that can is supranuclear (PPRF or cortex)
Gaze palsy plus peripheral facial palsy equals the facial colliculus
